vision:
The site's analytics are already stronger than most public vol tools. It scores models in half-spreads on held-out quotes, certifies static arbitrage, replicates the VIX from the chain, runs bootstrap/SPA/PBO inference, keeps a corrections ledger and shows a negative backtest as it is. What keeps it from being the best volatility research and model-validation site a Citadel reviewer has seen comes down to four things, which are also the four packages.

(1) A few things on the site currently mislead, and a reviewer would screenshot them:
- Research draws the two losing sleeves in the gain colour. I verified this in the browser: S1C −453.8 and S4 −273.7 both render #4c90f0, because desk.js reads the category string as the value on horizontal bars.
- Every signed KPI tile shows no colour (the .kpi-value rule overrides .pos/.neg).
- A 99.99% 'Hedge P&L explained' tile is a Taylor-remainder check.
- The calibration banner blames a quality gate, although no newer fit exists.
- The VVIX sentence is false on the headline session. The diagnostics show the σ≤10 refit matching VVIX at 112.7 vs 109.9 and cutting OOS from 2.96 to 1.19.
- The Overview showcases PDV without saying it ranks 6th of 7 on QLIKE. It also ranks 2nd of 7 on MSE, and the disclosure must state both.

(2) The site does not speak desk language. That means:
- 25Δ/10Δ risk reversals and butterflies (verified: 2026-11-16 ATMF 13.82, RR25 −5.82, BF25 +0.84);
- the ATM-skew power law that explains the Heston and rough-Heston results;
- implied against subsequently realized vol, plus what the β·VIX mark leaves of the premium (verified: mean −0.46 vol pts at β 0.82 over 2018-01-02 → 2025-03-24, against +3.11 at β 1);
- the VX futures leg. The committed fits' VX OOS RMSE (2.664 / 3.176 / 2.556 / 1.854) reproduces exactly from heston_vix_future_exact on vix_futures_daily monthly settles.

(3) Model Risk shows a snapshot, but SR 26-2 asks for persistence. Every check can be recomputed on the 5 stored sessions.

(4) Interaction mechanics:
- quote-level hover;
- linked views;
- a 300–450 ms smile switch at 4× CPU, caused by re-parsing a 247 KB spec and rebuilding 119 series;
- grid holes at 1024 px;
- one colour carrying several meanings.

Verification notes for the engineers:
- B2's α values labelled 'T ≥ 30 d' are in fact all-expiry fits. P2.2 lists both sets.
- Several anchors the reviews cite do not exist: #beta, #forecasts, model-risk #check-*. The real ids are #beta-chains, #beta-grid and #forecast; check ids must be created.
- Extending the β grid changes the trials ledger, so it is rejected.
- Browser behaviour checks go in a new scripts/ci/a11y/interact.mjs run by the existing a11y CI job.

Every new number comes from a committed artifact through a pure, unit-tested function. Every 'next' item is phrased as not done. Each 'does not work' finding gets the same prominence as each 'works' finding.

packages.title: Trust pass: fix what misleads, and tell the joint SPX/VIX story straight

items.title: P&L sign colour on signed bars and KPI tones, plus the keyboard-dialog position (from D1 and the craft summary item 5)
items.detail:
Signed bars, dashboard/static/desk.js buildSeries (line 129):
- The signed-bar callback reads `Array.isArray(p.value) ? p.value[1] : p.value`. buildOption has already swapped horizontal data to [value, category] (lines 230-234), so p.value[1] is the category string and every bar gets T.colors.pos.
- Fix: `var hz = !!spec.horizontal; ... var v = Array.isArray(p.value) ? p.value[hz ? 0 : 1] : p.value;`. spec is already a parameter.
- Verified in the browser on research.html #chart-sleeves: [-453.8 'S1C contrarian'], [61 'S3'] and [-273.7 'S4 VRP'] all render #4c90f0.

KPI tones, dashboard/static/desk.css:
- `.kpi-value { color: var(--text) }` (line 247) comes after `.pos/.neg` (lines 166-167) at equal specificity, so tone classes never show.
- Add `.kpi-value.pos, .result-v.pos, .param-val.pos { color: var(--pos) }`, plus the .neg equivalents.
- Affected tiles: risk.html 4 pos and 4 neg, research.html 2 neg, index.html 1 pos.
- The sign glyph stays, so colour is never the only cue.

Keyboard dialog:
- The universal reset `*, *::before, *::after { margin: 0 }` removes the UA centring of <dialog>. Measured: #keysDialog opens at left 0, top 0.
- Add `dialog.keys { margin: auto; }` (and `inset: 0` for the modal case).
items.acceptance:
1) New scripts/ci/a11y/interact.mjs, wired into the a11y job in .github/workflows/tests.yml. For every rendered chart whose spec has a series with signed:true, the fill of each item (chart.getModel().getSeriesByIndex(i).getData().getItemVisual(j,'style').fill) equals the --neg-fill colour when its value is < 0 and --pos-fill otherwise. On chart-sleeves this means S1C and S4 neg, S3 pos. The same check runs on chart-annual and every other signed spec.
2) Every .kpi-value.neg computes to rgb(251,179,96) and every .kpi-value.pos to rgb(138,187,255), on risk, research and index.
3) On surface.html at 1440 and 390, pressing '?' opens #keysDialog with |left − (viewport − width)/2| ≤ 2 px.

items.title: ATM-skew term structure on log–log axes: market power law against published Heston and the σ ≤ 10 refit, with exponents for all 5 sessions (B2 + Q2, numbers corrected)
items.detail:
New Calibration panel #skew-term after #oos. Surface's ATM-skew column (P2.1) links to it.

Series, with x = T in years on a log axis and y = |∂σ/∂k| at k = 0 on a log axis, labelled 'vol per unit ln-moneyness':
- Market SVI-cal analytic skew per slice: w′(0)/(2√(w(0)·T)) with w′(k) = b(ρ + (k−m)/√((k−m)² + σ²)). The headline session is solid; the other 4 sessions are thin and muted.
- Market eSSVI: stored term_structure.atm_skew_essvi, headline only, dotted. It differs from SVI-cal by about 40% at 31 d (−1.387 vs −1.008) because eSSVI's ψ(θ) shapes the term structure. Show both and say so.
- Heston at the published params: central finite difference ±0.01 in k with heston_model_smile(params, maturities_days = listed T, log_moneyness = (−0.01, 0, 0.01)).
- Heston at the σ ≤ 10 refit, using diagnostics sigma_profile.rows[-1].params (κ 27.39, σ 6.90), dashed.

Table: per session, the OLS slope of log|skew| on log T for SVI-cal and eSSVI, on all expiries and on T ≥ 30 d, with n and T range. Verified values:
- All expiries, SVI-cal: −0.409, −0.315, −0.336, −0.357, −0.450.
- All expiries, eSSVI: −0.439, −0.358, −0.392, −0.422, −0.557.
- T ≥ 30 d, SVI-cal: −0.465, −0.427, −0.310, −0.325, −0.467 (n 27/25/26/27/13).
- T ≥ 30 d, eSSVI: −0.493, −0.441, −0.415, −0.454, −0.583.
- Sessions in order: 03-24, 03-27, 05-29, 06-18, 10-16.
B2 labelled the all-expiry eSSVI values as 'T ≥ 30 d'.

Caption: 'inside a rough-volatility model the skew scales as T^(H−1/2); this is a descriptive slope of one fitted surface per session, sensitive to the shortest expiries and to the parametrisation, not an estimate of H (the rough-Heston H sits on its 0.02 floor)'.

Add a cross-link from #rough-vs-heston.
items.acceptance:

items.title: Implied against subsequently realized vol, and what the β·VIX mark leaves of the premium (B3 + the descriptive half of Q4)
items.detail:
New pure module dashboard/desk_market.py, reading vol_system.db spx_ohlcv.log_return and vix_daily.close (4,228 sessions, 2010-01-04 → 2026-10-23):
- rv_trailing(21);
- rv_forward(21), using the forecast_eval.json target definition √(252/21 · Σ r²) over t+1..t+21, so it matches the site's own forecast target;
- vrp(β) = β·VIX − RV21 forward;
- yearly means.

New Research panel #vrp next to #forecast:
- Chart: VIX, RV21 trailing, RV21 forward (ends 2026-09-24) and 0.82·VIX dashed.
- A second, linked chart: ex-post VRP at β = 1 as signed bars with a zero line.
- The backtest window 2018-01-02 → 2025-03-24 is shaded.
- S4 entry dates from full_results.pkl all_trades are marked (46: 22 short, 24 long).
- The existing 1Y/3Y/All presets apply.

Table for β ∈ {1.00, 0.82 (the backtest), 0.80, 0.70 (the newest chain's ATM/VIX)}, over the backtest window (n = 1,816): mean, median, share > 0 (vol pts) and the variance-space mean β²VIX² − RV² (vol pts²). Verified:
- β 1.00: +3.11 / +4.32 / 79.2% / +50.1
- β 0.82: −0.46 / +1.19 / 61.6% / −97.7
- β 0.80: −0.85 / +0.86 / 58.2% / −112.3
- β 0.70: −2.84 / −1.01 / 39.6% / −180.0

Also:
- Calendar-year bars of the β = 0.82 mean, using the in-flight YTD helper for 2025 (55 sessions).
- Full-sample line: mean ex-post VRP +3.75 vol pts, positive on 84.6% of sessions.
- Overview #state-pdv gains 'VIX − RV21 (trailing) +9.57 vol pts, 2026-10-23' (VIX 19.45 vs RV21 9.88).

Caption:
- VIX is a 30-calendar-day variance-swap rate including the skew premium, so VIX − RV overstates what an ATM straddle earns.
- 21-session windows overlap, so the shares are not counts of independent events; no t-stat is given.
- This is a description, not P&L, and does not 'explain' the backtest.

items.title: One meaning per colour, one name per model, units in every tooltip (D2 + D11 + the tooltip half of D10)
items.detail:
ENCODING registry in dashboard/desk_charts.py, used by every spec builder:
- per model: colour token, dash and label;
- per role: market observable, Cboe index, anchor, bid–ask.

Rules:
(1) One label per model everywhere: 'Heston' rather than 'Heston (v2 fit)' or 'Heston model'; 'SVI-cal' rather than 'SVI, calendar-ordered'.
(2) On a page that draws models, no other categorical series uses a model colour. Today the Calibration #chart-model-smile tenors use cat0, cat1 and cat4, the same as SVI-cal, Heston and eSSVI.
(3) Tenor-indexed series (#chart-model-smile, Risk flag chart) use a sequential lightness ramp ordered by T, with a gradient key.
(4) On P&L or return charts, no series is within ΔE76 < 25 of --pos-fill or --neg-fill. Today S3 is cat1 #e69f00, ΔE 16.6 from neg-fill. Use free palette slots with dashes and end-of-line labels.
(5) Market observables and Cboe indices use 'headline' everywhere. Overview #state-ts draws the VIX family in cat0 while Calibration #vixleg uses white.
(6) No series uses the 'info' token, which is identical to --pos #8abbff.

Heat ramps (desk_format.py):
- PNL_DIV only on P&L heatmaps (scenario, monthly).
- Residuals keep BERLIN_11, but its blue end #9EB0FF sits next to --pos, so swap it for a diverging ramp whose ends are neither P&L hues nor breach red, labelled 'model below mid ◀ 0 ▶ model above mid'.
- The vomma flag view uses cividis on the ratio 0 → 0.25 with the breach outline and ⚠. The ratio is the primary 12 px text and vomma the secondary text.
- No text inside table.heat is smaller than 10.5 px (today 9.5 px '.z' cells).
- Every ramp legend gets numeric endpoints and a unit.

Tooltip grammar (tooltipFor):
- the header carries the x label and unit, with index names where they exist ('VIX3M · 93 d', not '93.0');
- every row carries its unit ('3.89 vol pts').

rejected.why: Re-running the backtest at β = 0.70 and 0.75 changes research results, not just the UI. beta_sensitivity.csv feeds the trials ledger: test_stats_trials asserts the C22 family counts and that the β-grid configurations equal the CSV rows. scripts/inference_report.py also builds the PBO/SPA trial set from that CSV. Adding β rows would therefore move the published inference numbers and needs its own correction round. The descriptive β table in P3.2 answers the reviewer's question (β = 0.70 leaves −2.84 vol pts of premium) without touching the trial set.

Rejected: the '% of $1M NAV at the margin-cap size' readout in the scenario grid. No position the backtest held had that size, because Kelly overlays shrink positions, so the number invites being read as portfolio risk. P1.4 keeps the $ per SPX contract readout, which is a pure unit change.

Adding RV21, VIX−RV21, a percentile, 1M ATMF and RR25 to the global ticker conflicts with the chrome budget: the ticker already wraps to 3 lines at 390 px and main starts at y = 164. It would also mix as-of dates (market 2026-10-23, surface 2026-10-16) in the site chrome. These numbers land in their panels with their own dates: P2.1 (Surface state row, plus the Overview line) and P3.2 (Overview VIX − RV21 line).

Low value. A line chart of the existing scenario grid for a generic reference straddle repeats numbers the grid already prints. P1.4 adds $ units and P4.5 recolours the grid; neither adds information.

It would re-price 2018–2025 backtest positions under spot/vol shocks with the same β·VIX Black–Scholes mark whose validity is the open question (P3.2). That adds a third modelled layer and no market information, and a reader could take it for live book risk.
Q19's 252-session 10–90% band per tenor on the 4-point VIX curve is clutter. Its useful parts are merged into P3.5: dated overlays, the VIX/VIX3M percentile and the VVIX-to-R2-gate distance.

The per-sleeve table and P&L-by-sleeve chart already answer the headline question. Revisit after P3.6.
